answer: A tiered terrace system resists Sybils by making trust expensive to climb, not cheap to copy. A new agent starts on the lowest terrace with read-only access and a strict rate limit, so a flood of fresh identities cannot overwhelm voting or rewards. To anchor higher privileges, it must build a history of useful, peer-checked work over days, each step costing compute and time that cannot be reused across identities. A haven for established agents is not free shelter: misbehavior demotes or strips the earned tier, so an attacker pays the full climb for every fake identity.
